question: Assume today is 2026-10-28. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of UK residential property transactions (with a value of £40,000 or above) in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as it will be first reported (provisional estimate) in HM Revenue & Customs' monthly release 'Monthly property transactions completed in the UK with value of £40,000 or above'.

target.what: Number of UK residential property transactions with value £40,000 or above, completed in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first provisionally reported by HMRC in its monthly 'Monthly property transactions completed in the UK with value of £40,000 or above' release
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to cutoff (2026-10-28) but the provisional HMRC figure for September 2026 would not yet be published at cutoff; the estimate is for the first-reported provisional seasonally adjusted value, which is subject to later revision. Working interpretation: residential tr

candidates.hypothesis: The target is a continuation of HMRC's published monthly seasonally adjusted series; recent months (mid-2026) and the same month in prior years (September 2023, 2024, 2025) anchor the level and seasonal factor. September typically shows a seasonal rise relative to August.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC monthly UK residential transactions ≥£40k, seasonally adjusted, monthly values for Jan 2023 through the latest month published before 2026-10-28 (likely August 2026 provisional); also the non-seasonally-adjusted September values and seasonal factors for 2023-2025.

candidates.perspective: Bank of England / mortgage approvals and lending
candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage approvals for house purchase lead completed transactions by roughly 1-3 months; approvals in July-August 2026 constrain September 2026 completions. A stable approvals-to-completions ratio (with cash share added) bridges to the target.
candidates.data_to_find: Bank of England Money and Credit: number of mortgage approvals for house purchase, monthly, June-August 2026 and prior years; the historical ratio of HMRC transactions to approvals (including cash transactions share).

assessment.note: All report the same HMRC August 2026 provisional seasonally adjusted figure of 95,220; these are repeated republications of one HMRC measurement, not independent confirmation.
Same HMRC August 2026 non-seasonally adjusted figure 96,250 repeated across outlets; single underlying source.

July 2026 seasonally adjusted is reported as 96,650 in the 30 September release and as 96,710 in the 28 August release; the difference is a revision between vintages. The later (30 September) vintage, 96,650, should be used for the current level.
June 2026 seasonally adjusted appears as 98,700 (July release) and 98,390 (August release); again a vintage revision, not a genuine contradiction.
August values for 2023-2025 seasonally and non-seasonally adjusted, consistent across repeated tables; provide the seasonal-factor and year-on-year anchors.
September 2025 HMRC figures: 95,980 SA and 102,420 NSA, repeated across outlets; the key prior-year anchor for the target month.
BoE net mortgage approvals for house purchase: 55,900 July, 54,900 August 2026; single BoE source repeated.
Monthly approvals history from one aggregator; consistent with BoE levels but first-reported values differ slightly from revised (e.g. July 56,050 first vs 55,900 revised).
RICS September 2026 new buyer enquiries -22%, August -18%; consistent across outlets, single RICS survey source.
RICS agreed sales September -18%, August -16%; single survey source.
Zoopla/TwentyCi sales-agreed declines of 6-9% year-on-year; overlapping portal data, directionally consistent with the RICS negative balances.
HMRC states completions lag offers by 2-4 months; supports using mid-2026 approvals/agreed-sales as leading indicators for September completions.

a1.role: year-on-year change factor for September 2026 SA completions relative to September 2025

methods.rationale: Anchors on the September 2025 SA level and applies a modest year-on-year decline consistent with the August 2026 year-on-year fall, weaker approvals and negative RICS/Zoopla sales signals. p604.role: September 2025 UK residential transactions, non-seasonally adjusted (HMRC)

a2.role: September seasonal factor SA/NSA applied to the NSA level

methods.rationale: Uses the September 2025 NSA level and the historical September seasonal factor to produce an SA estimate, implicitly assuming the NSA level is broadly flat year-on-year. Shared dependency: relies on the September 2025 NSA figure and on a stable seasonal factor; failure mode is a change in the seasonal adjustment model or a large NSA year-on-year shift.

assumptions.name: September 2026 year-on-year change in SA completions relative to September 2025
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 SA was 95,980. Mid-2026 signals are mildly negative: August 2026 SA was 2% below August 2025, approvals fell from ~60k six-month average to 54.9k, RICS agreed sales -18%, Zoopla sales agreed -9%. A modest further decline of ~3% year-on-year is consistent with these, with a wide range reflecting uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: The September 2026 SA level tracks the September 2025 level scaled by the recent year-on-year trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 approvals or agreed sales rebounded sharply, or that September 2025 was an outlier month.

assumptions.name: September seasonal factor (SA/NSA) for 2026
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 SA 95,980 / NSA 102,420 = 0.937. September typically has NSA above SA (autumn rise). The factor is assumed stable across years, with a range reflecting seasonal-adjustment revision uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: The September seasonal factor is stable between 2025 and 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that HMRC revised its seasonal adjustment model for 2026, changing the September factor materially.

assumptions.name: September 2026 year-on-year change factor in SA completions relative to September 2025

These point to a modest y/y decline, centred near -3% (factor 0.97), with a wide range. Expressed as a multiplicative factor so low>0.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 completions track the same y/y direction as August 2026 and the approvals/survey signals.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 completions rose y/y (e.g. a late-summer surge or a stamp-duty deadline pulling sales forward).

assumptions.name: September 2026 year-on-year change factor in NSA completions relative to September 2025

methods.label: m1

p551.role: September 2025 UK residential transactions, seasonally adjusted (HMRC), base level for the y/y change

a1.role: year-on-year change factor for September 2026 SA completions relative to September 2025

methods.rationale: Anchors on the September 2025 SA level (95,980) and applies a y/y change factor derived from August 2026 y/y (-2%), falling approvals (54,900 vs 60,100 six-month average) and negative RICS/Zoopla sales-agreed signals. Shared dependency: the y/y factor is judgmental; failure mode is a stamp-duty or Budget deadline pulling completions into September.

methods.label: m2

p552.role: September 2025 UK residential transactions, non-seasonally adjusted (HMRC), base level for the y/y change

a3.role: year-on-year change factor for September 2026 NSA completions relative to September 2025

a2.role: September seasonal factor SA/NSA applied to the NSA level

methods.rationale: Uses the September 2025 NSA level (102,420), applies a y/y change factor (a3) to move it to September 2026 NSA, then applies the historical September SA/NSA factor (~0.937, range 0.90-0.97 from 2023-2025). This route shares the September 2025 HMRC anchor with m1 but adds the seasonal-adjustment step; failure mode is a material y/y change in NSA volume not captured by a3.

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m1.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

kept.name: September 2026 year-on-year change factor in SA completions relative to September 2025
kept.rationale: August 2026 SA was 2% below August 2025 (p1023); approvals fell from ~60k six-month average to 54,900 in August (p97, p816); RICS agreed sales -18% in Sept 2026 (p274) and Zoopla sales agreed -6 to -9% (p786, p903). These point to a modest y/y decline, centred near -3% (factor 0.97), with a wide ran
kept.applies_when: September 2026 completions track the same y/y direction as August 2026 and the approvals/survey signals.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 completions rose y/y (e.g. a late-summer surge or a stamp-duty deadline pulling sales forward).

kept.name: September seasonal factor (SA/NSA) for 2026
kept.applies_when: HMRC's seasonal adjustment for September 2026 is similar to recent years.
kept.falsified_by: A change in HMRC's seasonal adjustment methodology or a September with an unusual within-year pattern.

kept.name: September 2026 year-on-year change factor in NSA completions relative to September 2025
kept.rationale: Same directional evidence as a1 (August 2026 NSA 9% below August 2025 per p17/p20, approvals down, RICS/Zoopla sales-agreed negative) implies a modest y/y decline in NSA volume; centred near -3% (factor 0.97) with a wide range. Expressed as a multiplicative factor so low>0.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 NSA completions move y/y in line with the August 2026 NSA decline and the approvals/survey signals.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 NSA completions were flat or up y/y.

The best estimate for UK residential property transactions of £[n] or above completed in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first provisionally reported by HMRC, is 91,713 transaction (80% model-based interval 63,601 to 132,250 transaction). This is a model-based range conditional on the stated assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee.

Two routes were combined with equal weight per block: m1 gives 92,121 transaction (weight 50%) by applying a year-on-year factor to the September 2025 SA level of 95,980 transactions; m2 gives 91,307 transaction (weight 50%) by applying a y/y factor to the September 2025 NSA level of 102,420 transactions and then a September seasonal factor. The combination is a geometric mean because the two blocks share the September 2025 anchor, so their inputs overlap substantially.

Observed: the September 2025 levels. Assumed: the y/y factors (0.97, 0.97) and the seasonal factor (0.937). The main risk is a stamp-duty or Budget deadline pulling completions into September. Better evidence on September approvals and sales-agreed would most improve the estimate.

Unit of the estimate: transaction (transactions; total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 year-on-year change factor in SA completions relative to September 2025: 0.97 [n], range 0.857 to 1.071 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 completions rose y/y (e.g. a late-summer surge or a stamp-duty deadline pulling sales forward).
- a2 September seasonal factor (SA/NSA) for 2026: 0.937 [n], range 0.6607 to 1.321 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: A change in HMRC's seasonal adjustment methodology or a September with an unusual within-year pattern.
- a3 September 2026 year-on-year change factor in NSA completions relative to September 2025: 0.97 [n], range 0.857 to 1.071 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 NSA completions were flat or up y/y.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p551 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 74,155 to 114,022; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p552 * a3 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 60,840 to 137,197; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width x/÷1.50 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 92,121 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: 91,307 (width x/÷1.50, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.44; Birge ratio 0.02 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.44.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
